why: The answer uses a rule that contradicts Java, namely that toUpperCase changes the String in name, and so predicts JAVA when the program actually prints java.

concepts.why: Strings are immutable: toUpperCase returns a new String and leaves name as "java".
A method call that returns a value does not change the object it is called on, and here the returned value is thrown away because the call stands on its own as a statement.
The answer says nothing about how println works; it only gets the wrong value of name.
The answer makes no claim about the source text, the file or compiling.
